title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 19
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Five candidates sat two papers. The final mark is 60% of paper one and 40% of paper two:

Ardley: paper one 72, paper two 88
Brayton: paper one 85, paper two 64
Caldon: paper one 68, paper two 92
Delph: paper one 91, paper two 58
Erridge: paper one 79, paper two 76

Which candidate has the highest final mark?
options: A. Brayton
B. Caldon
C. Delph
D. Erridge
E. Ardley
questions.explanation: Weighting each pair: Ardley 78.4, Brayton 76.6, Caldon 77.6, Delph 77.8, Erridge 77.8. Ardley finishes top at 78.4 without winning either paper: Delph leads paper one with 91 and Caldon leads paper two with 92. A strong second on the heavier paper beats a first on the lighter one.

questions.prompt:
Annual figures:

2015: 210
2016: 224
2017: 219
2018: 231
2019: 246
2020: 258
2021: 240
2022: 252
2023: 261
2024: 255

What is the longest run of consecutive years in which the figure rose?
options: A. Two
B. Four
C. Three
D. Five
E. The figure never rose twice in a row
questions.explanation: Year on year the figure rises, falls, rises, rises, rises, falls, rises, rises, falls. The longest unbroken run of rises is 3, ending in 2020. There is a run of two later on, but nothing longer.

questions.prompt:
A household budget of GBP 2,850.00 a month, by category:

Housing: 34%
Transport: 17%
Food: 22%
Energy: 11%
Other: not shown

How much goes on "Other" each month?
questions.explanation: The four named categories account for 84% of the budget, so "Other" is the remaining 16%. 16% of GBP 2,850.00 is GBP 456.00. The figure is not printed anywhere in the table — it has to be found as what is left when the rest is taken away.

questions.prompt:
Eight readings, in order: 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 30

Which statement about these readings is accurate?
options: A. The mean is greater than the median, which is greater than the mode
B. The mode is greater than the median
C. The mean and the median are equal
D. The median is greater than the mean
E. All three measures are equal
questions.explanation: Mean 9.75, median 6.5, mode 5. The single reading of 30 drags the mean well above the middle of the data while leaving the median and the mode where they are. Mean above median above mode is the signature of a set with a long tail to the right, and it is why the median is usually quoted for incomes and house prices.

questions.prompt:
A firm turns over GBP 1,800,000.00 a year and spends 45% of that on wages for its 60 staff.

Select the wage bill AND the average wage.
options: A. GBP 810,000.00 in wages; GBP 30,000.00 each
B. GBP 990,000.00 in wages; GBP 13,500.00 each
C. GBP 810,000.00 in wages; GBP 15,000.00 each
D. GBP 810,000.00 in wages; GBP 13,500.00 each
E. The average wage cannot be worked out from what is given
questions.explanation: 45% of GBP 1,800,000.00 is GBP 810,000.00, and shared between 60 staff that averages GBP 13,500.00. Dividing the whole turnover by the headcount gives GBP 30,000.00, which is turnover a head rather than pay.

questions.prompt:
A monthly rent rises from GBP 940.00 to GBP 1,081.00.

Select the percentage increase AND the extra amount payable over a full year.
options: A. 15%; GBP 141.00 more over the year
B. 15%; GBP 1,692.00 more over the year
C. 13.04%; GBP 1,692.00 more over the year
D. 15%; GBP 1,410.00 more over the year
E. 13.04%; GBP 141.00 more over the year
questions.explanation: The rent rises by GBP 141.00, which against the old GBP 940.00 is 15%. Over twelve months that is GBP 141.00 × 12 = GBP 1,692.00. Measuring the rise against the new rent gives 13.04%, and quoting GBP 141.00 as the annual figure counts a single month.

questions.prompt:
Two consultants worked on the same project:

Consultant One: GBP 145.00 an hour, 12 hours
Consultant Two: GBP 96.00 an hour, 22 hours

Select the consultant on the higher hourly rate AND the consultant whose total fee was larger.
options: A. Consultant One on both measures
B. Consultant Two on both measures
C. Consultant Two on the hourly rate; Consultant One on the total fee
D. The two fees are equal
E. Consultant One on the hourly rate; Consultant Two on the total fee
questions.explanation: Hourly rates are given: Consultant One GBP 145.00, Consultant Two GBP 96.00. Total fees are rate multiplied by hours: Consultant One GBP 1,740.00 and Consultant Two GBP 2,112.00. The dearer consultant billed barely half as many hours, so the cheaper one cost more in the end.

questions.prompt:
Fixed costs are GBP 7,200.00 a year. Each unit sells for GBP 34.00 and costs GBP 16.00 to make.

Select the number of units needed to break even AND the profit at 600 units.
options: A. 211.765 units to break even; GBP 3,600.00 at 600
B. 400 units to break even; GBP 13,200.00 at 600
C. 400 units to break even; GBP 3,600.00 at 600
D. 400 units to break even; GBP 10,800.00 at 600
E. The business cannot break even at any volume
questions.explanation: Each unit contributes GBP 34.00 − GBP 16.00 = GBP 18.00 towards the fixed costs, so breaking even takes GBP 7,200.00 / GBP 18.00 = 400 units. At 600 units the contribution totals GBP 10,800.00, leaving GBP 3,600.00 once the fixed costs are met. Dividing the fixed costs by the selling price gives 211.765 units and forgets that each unit costs something to make.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): inmates held — Prison P 1,120, Prison Q 640, Prison R 1,850

SOURCE 2 (table): officers on the roll — Prison P 280, Prison Q 130, Prison R 420

SOURCE 3 (memo): "The new staff go to whichever prison holds the most inmates for each officer it already has."

Which prison receives the new staff?
options: A. Prison Q
B. Prison P
C. Prison R
D. The three prisons are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Inmates divided by officers: Prison P 4, Prison Q 4.92, Prison R 4.4. Prison Q is stretched thinnest and is the smallest prison. Prison R holds 1,850 inmates, more than any other, but has 420 officers.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "The overall pass rate fell from 75% to 68%."

SOURCE 2 (table): the day cohort's pass rate rose from 80% to 83%, and the evening cohort's from 55% to 58%.

SOURCE 3 (table): the evening cohort grew from 20% of all candidates to 60%.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Both cohorts did worse than before
B. The day cohort did worse than before
C. The overall fall shows that standards slipped
D. The evening cohort shrank as a share of candidates
E. Both cohorts improved, and the overall rate fell only because the lower-scoring cohort grew as a share of the whole
questions.explanation: Every group in the table improved: the day cohort by 3 points and the evening cohort by 3. The overall figure still fell because the evening cohort, which passes at a lower rate, went from 20% of candidates to 60%. An average across groups can move against every group in it when the mix between them changes.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): daily rate — Venue A GBP 1,250.00, Venue B GBP 1,480.00, Venue C GBP 1,340.00

SOURCE 2 (table): availability — Venue A is booked from 8 to 20 September; Venues B and C are free all month.

SOURCE 3 (email): "We need a venue for the week beginning 14 September, at the lowest cost."

Which venue should be booked?
options: A. Venue A
B. Venue B
C. All three cost the same
D. Venue C
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Venue A is cheapest at GBP 1,250.00 a day but is booked across the whole of the week beginning 14 September, so its rate never comes into play. Of the two free that week, Venue B at GBP 1,480.00 and Venue C at GBP 1,340.00, Venue C is cheaper by GBP 140.00 a day.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): the fund grew from GBP 4.2 million to GBP 5.6 million over the year.

SOURCE 2 (memo): "The target for the year was GBP 5 million."

SOURCE 3 (note): the fund manager changed in March.

The question is whether the fund met its target. Which source adds nothing to answering it?
options: A. Source 1, the fund's value
B. Source 3, the change of manager
C. Source 2, the target
D. None of them: all three are needed
E. Sources 2 and 3 are both unnecessary
questions.explanation: Whether the target was met needs the final value and the target: GBP 5.6 million against GBP 5 million, so it was, by GBP 600,000. Who was managing the fund at the time bears on why it grew, not on whether it cleared the bar. A source can be interesting and still be irrelevant to the question asked.

questions.prompt:
What is the perimeter of an equilateral triangle?

(1) One of its sides measures 14 cm.
(2) Its height is 7 times the square root of 3 centimetres.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: All three sides of an equilateral triangle are equal, so (1) gives a perimeter of 3 × 14 = 42 cm. The height of an equilateral triangle is the side times the square root of 3, divided by 2, so (2) gives a side of 14 and the same perimeter. Each statement alone is enough.

questions.prompt:
Is x greater than y?

(1) x − y = 5
(2) x + y = 20
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: A difference of 5 means x sits 5 above y whatever their values, so (1) answers the question with a yes. (2) fits x = 15 and y = 5 as readily as x = 5 and y = 15, so it settles nothing. The two are consistent, giving x = 12.5 and y = 7.5.

questions.prompt:
For how many hours did a machine run?

(1) It used 84 litres of fuel.
(2) It uses 7 litres of fuel an hour.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives the fuel but no rate, and (2) gives the rate but no quantity. Together, 84 litres at 7 litres an hour is 12 hours. Each statement supplies exactly one of the two things the calculation needs.

questions.prompt:
What is the value of a two-digit number?

(1) Its digits add to 9.
(2) It is divisible by 3.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) admits 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81 and 90 — nine candidates. Every one of them is divisible by 9 and therefore by 3, so (2) removes none of them. A second statement that is automatically true of everything the first allows narrows nothing at all.

questions.prompt:
Which operator carries the most passengers for each vessel it runs?

Operator | Vessels | Routes | Passengers (thousands) | On time
Ashlyn | 6 | 4 | 1,240 | 86%
Brentmoor | 14 | 9 | 3,180 | 79%
Corrow | 3 | 2 | 640 | 93%
Dunbrae | 26 | 12 | 5,400 | 74%
Ellerby | 9 | 6 | 2,400 | 88%
Fenwold | 4 | 3 | 910 | 91%
options: A. Ashlyn
B. Ellerby
C. Brentmoor
D. Dunbrae
E. Fenwold
questions.explanation: Passengers divided by vessels: Ashlyn 207 thousand, Brentmoor 227 thousand, Corrow 213 thousand, Dunbrae 208 thousand, Ellerby 267 thousand, Fenwold 228 thousand. Ellerby works its fleet hardest at 267 thousand a vessel. Dunbrae carries 5,400 thousand passengers, more than twice as many, but runs 26 vessels to do it.

questions.prompt:
Which operator carries the most passengers on each route it runs?

Operator | Vessels | Routes | Passengers (thousands) | On time
Ashlyn | 6 | 4 | 1,240 | 86%
Brentmoor | 14 | 9 | 3,180 | 79%
Corrow | 3 | 2 | 640 | 93%
Dunbrae | 26 | 12 | 5,400 | 74%
Ellerby | 9 | 6 | 2,400 | 88%
Fenwold | 4 | 3 | 910 | 91%
options: A. Ashlyn
B. Brentmoor
C. Dunbrae
D. Corrow
E. Ellerby
questions.explanation: Passengers divided by routes: Ashlyn 310 thousand, Brentmoor 353 thousand, Corrow 320 thousand, Dunbrae 450 thousand, Ellerby 400 thousand, Fenwold 303 thousand. Dunbrae carries the most on each route at 450 thousand. That is a different operator from Ellerby, which carries the most per vessel — the two ratios rank the same six operators differently because routes and vessels are not shared out in the same proportions.

questions.prompt:
How many operators run at 85% on time or better?

Operator | Vessels | Routes | Passengers (thousands) | On time
Ashlyn | 6 | 4 | 1,240 | 86%
Brentmoor | 14 | 9 | 3,180 | 79%
Corrow | 3 | 2 | 640 | 93%
Dunbrae | 26 | 12 | 5,400 | 74%
Ellerby | 9 | 6 | 2,400 | 88%
Fenwold | 4 | 3 | 910 | 91%
options: A. Four
B. Two
C. Three
D. Five
E. One
questions.explanation: On-time figures: Ashlyn 86%, Brentmoor 79%, Corrow 93%, Dunbrae 74%, Ellerby 88%, Fenwold 91%. At 85% or above: Ashlyn, Corrow, Ellerby, Fenwold — 4 operators. The two that fall short are the two largest fleets in the table.

questions.prompt:
How many operators are above the median on punctuality and below the median on passengers?

Operator | Vessels | Routes | Passengers (thousands) | On time
Ashlyn | 6 | 4 | 1,240 | 86%
Brentmoor | 14 | 9 | 3,180 | 79%
Corrow | 3 | 2 | 640 | 93%
Dunbrae | 26 | 12 | 5,400 | 74%
Ellerby | 9 | 6 | 2,400 | 88%
Fenwold | 4 | 3 | 910 | 91%
options: A. One
B. Three
C. Four
D. Two
E. Five
questions.explanation: The medians are 87% on time and 1,820 thousand passengers. Above on punctuality: Corrow, Ellerby, Fenwold. Below on passengers: Ashlyn, Corrow, Fenwold. On both: Corrow and Fenwold — 2. The smaller operators are the punctual ones here, though not every one of them clears the median.
